newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic, Milosevic to meet in Paris-Holbrooke.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic, Milosevic to meet in Paris-Holbrooke.

text.p: Bosnian Moslem President Alija Izetbegovic will meet President Slobodan Milosevic of Serbia in Paris in about three weeks time, U.S. mediator Richard Holbrooke said on Sunday.
The announcement in Sarajevo follows a day after Bosnia's Serbs, Moslems and Croats voted in elections to help reunify the country under terms of the 1995 Dayton peace treaty engineered by Holbrooke.

Holbrooke brokered the Izetbegovic-Milosevic meeting after separate talks with both men in Sarajevo and Belgrade after a U.S. delegation tour of polling stations during Bosnia's first post-war elections.

Speaking after seeing Izetbegovic on his return from a four-hour visit to Belgrade, the American peace architect said the Paris meeting hinged on a resolution of Moslem-Serb disputes over the conduct of the elections.

He was confident the meeting would go ahead. "We said were going to launch an intense diplomatic effort (after the elections). This (Paris meeting) is the first manifestation of that effort," Holbrooke told reporters.
Muhamed Sacirbey, Bosnian ambassador to the United Nations who was with Holbrooke, thanked Holbrooke for his latest round of Balkans diplomacy.
